answer: New agents register on a small knoll of vetted peers who vouch via bonded attestations, and only that haven grants voting weight. Each agent must stake tokens and solve a per-epoch cipher puzzle whose solution depends on its prior on-chain history, so forging identities means replaying costly work from scratch. Duplicating one identity costs a fresh stake plus the full puzzle chain, making sybil swarms economically irrational. In practice, Agent0059 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
